blogs.title: When 'Type 2' Doesn't Fit: Navigating the Diagnostic Maze of MODY
blogs.description: This post explores the diagnostic challenge of differentiating Maturity-Onset Diabetes of the Young (MODY) from Type 1 and Type 2 Diabetes. We discuss the 'red flags' for monogenic diabetes—such as early onset, negative autoantibodies, and strong family history—and why traditional markers like BMI and metabolic syndrome may be increasingly unreliable as obesity rates rise in all populations.

blogs.title: Beyond the Database: Interpreting Novel Mutations in Precision Medicine
blogs.description: What do you do when a patient’s genetic test reveals a mutation never before reported in ClinVar or VarSome? This post dives into the clinical reasoning required to interpret novel variants using ACMG guidelines, focusing on how family segregation, AlphaMissense scores, and known protein domains can confirm a diagnosis of HNF1A-MODY even in the absence of prior literature.

blogs.title: Moving Beyond Insulin: Tailoring Pharmacotherapy for HNF1A-MODY
blogs.description: In HNF1A-MODY, the goal of therapy is to manage glucose while preserving what remains of the patient's beta-cell function. We analyze the clinical shift from insulin to GLP-1 receptor agonists and sulfonylureas, discussing how C-peptide levels guide these decisions and why GLP-1 RAs offer a safer profile regarding hypoglycemia in this specific patient population.

blogs.title: The SGLT2 Inhibitor Trap: A Specific Warning for HNF1A Mutations
blogs.description: This post highlights a critical safety pearl: the unique pathophysiology of HNF1A-MODY. Because HNF1A transcriptionally regulates SGLT2, these patients may have a reduced renal glucose threshold and a higher risk of severe dehydration or DKA when treated with SGLT2 inhibitors. We discuss why these medications might carry a risk-to-benefit ratio that outweighs their typical utility in other diabetes types.

blogs.title: Small Fibers and Sweetness: Autonomic Dysfunction in Monogenic Diabetes
blogs.description: While hyperglycemia is the primary concern, this case reveals significant autonomic dysfunction via sudomotor testing. This post examines the significance of small-fiber nerve activity in MODY and how non-invasive tools like electrochemical skin conductance testing can provide a more complete picture of the systemic impact of monogenic mutations.
